h1: Roof Coating Services in Mission, TX
lede: Edel Roofing & Construction coats aging flat roofs on Mission businesses so the roof lasts longer and less heat comes through. The inspection is free, and you get a straight answer on whether your roof qualifies.

sections.title: Roof coatings for Mission businesses
paras: Mission has two kinds of commercial roofs right now. New buildings near the Bryan Rd corridor and Sharyland Business Park have new membranes that do not need a coating yet. Older retail and office buildings along Business 83 and Expressway 83 have roofs that have taken years of Valley sun, and some of those are good coating candidates.

A coating is a reflective liquid layer applied over the existing roof. It does not replace the roof. It covers a membrane that's still sound. It seals small cracks and seams and reflects heat, and that can buy you years before a tear off.

sections.title: Why Mission roofs age fast
paras: Heat and sun do most of the damage. NOAA normals for the McAllen airport, the closest official station to Mission, show 177 days a year at 90°F or hotter. Under that sun, a dark flat roof dries out, seams open, and the surface cracks.

Storms add to it. Hurricane Hanna dropped 14.40 inches of rain on Mission in 2020, and the 2016 downburst brought winds the NWS estimated at 85 to 95 mph. After events like those, a roof can hold water in its insulation or have loose edges that a coating cannot fix. So any coating job here starts with checking for wet insulation and loose membrane.

sections.title: What we check before coating a Mission roof

cards.title: Wet insulation
cards.body: We look for soft or damp areas. Wet insulation has to be cut out and replaced before any coating goes on.

cards.title: Seams and flashing
cards.body: Open seams and worn flashing get repaired so the coating has a sound surface to seal.

cards.title: Ponding areas
cards.body: We mark the spots where water sits after rain. Standing water changes which coating works and how long it lasts.

cards.title: Drains and edges
cards.body: Blocked drains and loose edge metal are fixed first, since a coating does not hold a loose roof down.

sections.title: Coating, repair, or replacement?
paras: If the membrane is dry, attached, and only worn on the surface, a coating usually makes sense and costs a fraction of a new roof. If the roof has leaks in many places, large wet areas, or is coming loose, the money is better spent on commercial roof repair or replacement in Mission. We tell you which one we see and why, in writing.

Most Mission homes are single family houses with pitched shingle roofs (about 68% of the city's housing, per Census survey data), and coatings are not made for those. For a house, see roof repair in Mission.

faqs.q: My building is new. Should I coat the roof now?
faqs.a: Usually not. A new membrane is still working fine. A coating makes more sense once the roof shows age, and an inspection every year or two tells you when that is.

faqs.q: Can you coat over a roof that got wet in a storm?
faqs.a: Not until the wet insulation is found and replaced. Coating over trapped water keeps it in the roof. We check for moisture first.

faqs.q: How much life does a coating add?
faqs.a: Several years, depending on the product, how thick it goes on, and the condition of the roof underneath. We give you a realistic number for your roof.

faqs.q: Will a coating lower my cooling bill?
faqs.a: A reflective surface reduces how much heat the roof absorbs, which can lower the temperature and cooling costs in the space below. How much depends on the building and its insulation.

faqs.q: How do I get a coating estimate in Mission?
faqs.a: Call (956) 422-3335 or book an inspection online. We are about 26 minutes from Mission, and the inspection and estimate are free.
